# Hello Clause

## Meaning
A root-local Connected Clause with one reusable action, `say`. Its body records text at a configured destination and emits `Hello Said`. Connections determine invocation; the type assigns no fixed actor or personal obligation.

## Configuration
- `bindings.text` is required and has no default path. It identifies the replacement destination. Planning requires a Text pointer beginning with `/` and different from `/`; no initial destination value is supplied.
- The action argument `text` defaults to `Hello World`. Connection `params` override action defaults. Trigger fields are not automatically copied into arguments; configure expressions when needed.
- Named connections for `say` select `event`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `channel`, `initialized`, `activated`, `workflow`, or `timer`. The type supplies no automatic connection. Clause and connection names must be nonempty Text without `.`, `/`, or `~`; unknown bindings and unsupported connection fields are rejected.
- Connection `when` defaults to true, `once` to false, and `before`/`after` hooks to empty lists. The optional per-action condition for `say` defaults to true; conditions naming undeclared actions are rejected.

The inherited transition check requires an existing clause key's configuration to remain unchanged; changed configuration requires a new clause key.

## Behavior
An already-fired `once` connection skips execution. Collection connections also skip events whose source path is outside the configured collection's descendants. After constructing arguments, a false `when` skips execution; a false per-action condition fails with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`.

The configured `before` hooks run before the action body. The body rejects a non-Text argument with `Hello text must be Text`, then appends a `replace` change at `bindings.text` and a `Hello Said` event containing the effective text, clause key, and connection key. The `after` hooks follow; for `once`, the workflow then appends `fired=true`. Hooks can add effects. These are declared local effects, not confirmation that an external recipient received or displayed the text. Event authority depends on authenticated input or document origin, not the event name.

Workflow connections use `party` when supplied, otherwise `channel`, and require a valid channel name. Channel sources require a named existing channel. Embedded and collection sources request embedding unless `embed` is false; change and embedded-source paths must be non-root pointers. Initialization and activation selectors target `Clauses Initialized` and `Document Activated`, respectively.

Timer connections require exactly one of an absolute Unix timestamp in microseconds or an `afterEvent` source with positive integer `delayMs`. Absolute timestamps range from 0 to 9007199254740991 and disallow delay and policy fields. Relative delays are at most 9007199254740 milliseconds, require a timestamped source rather than initialization, and must produce a deadline within the timestamp limit. Relative policy defaults to `first`, which skips another arm while `armed` is true; `latest` permits another arm request. Arming records `armed=true`; optional `cancelOn` emits a cancellation request without clearing that flag in the supplied code. Scheduling and cancellation requests do not confirm their external outcomes.

## State
The value addressed by `bindings.text` is the text destination. Its presence alone does not prove this action wrote it. Absence means unknown, not `Hello World` or proof that invocation never occurred; the greeting default applies only to action input.

## Limitations
The supplied definitions do not establish authentication enforcement, dispatch, commit atomicity, replacement of a missing destination, or timer runtime guarantees.
